## Summary

New data from Tussell reveals that UK public bodies spent £3.4bn on private consultants last year, representing a 62% increase compared to 2019-20. Despite the end of the pandemic, consultant spending has not returned to pre-Covid levels, posing a significant challenge for Keir Starmer's government, which has pledged to halve such expenditure during this parliament.

Since Labour came to power, nearly £650m in new government contracts have been awarded to consultants, including a notable deal worth up to £223m with KPMG to deliver civil service training over 15 months — many of these agreements were arranged before the change in government.

Labour peer and finance academic Prem Sikka has criticized the practice as "scandalous," arguing that a pervasive culture of hiring consultants has taken hold despite their limited ability to meaningfully understand and address the complexities of organizations in short engagements.
